question: Why the fall-back sends two of three defenders in an hour.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_FallBackFromLosingDefences
addresses.comment:
**Pulls defenders out of a losing battle.** 0x4D7F80 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D858B; always answers false. Only with the frontier at war and a unit. For each ops-area province p that is not its own depot and has a fort level below 3: for each land battle there (slot 11 == 1) at least 12 hours old (25 at plan stance 3 or more, CCombat +0x1C) in which we are a defending country (defender +0x54) and the attacker's share (slot 17) is above 0.7: p's neighbours (edge kind not 3, land, simulated) are scored - a hostile one across a river (kind 1 or 2) ends the look at this battle; one we may operate in scores effective infrastructure/1000 + 2 x fort level, +10 across a river, +100 if it is p's depot, and /100 if it is in the ops area; if no friendly land unit is already heading into p from a neighbour, the defenders without a blocking order are sent one each, best first, round the list again while defenders remain - **except that, where any candidate lies outside the ops area, reaching the first ops-area candidate ends the sending altogether** (its record's float +4 is 10.0, tested against 1.0 at 0x4D84DD, `ja` past the loop), so the list is gone round again only when the walk ran off its end (0x4D8532) (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 118: the July 1941 save's 1809 sends two of three defenders at 15:00 on 17 July and the third an hour later) - with a plain MoveUnit(unit, q, 0, 0, 0, 0), and full_pass_pending (+0x84) set. The name is ours.

**Read again on the listing, 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 24). A river is an edge of kind 1 **or** 2, and only across one is the neighbour's controller asked CCountry::IsEnemy (war or REB), which ends the look at the battle. For every land, simulated neighbour, each unit standing in it that is a land unit, whose owner the country may operate in (CCountry::CanOperateIn) and whose destination (0x89AF00) is the province is counted, and any such unit keeps the defenders in - it is a unit beside the province, not one anywhere. A neighbour is scored only where CanOperateIn answers for its controller. The defenders are the side's land units without UnitHasBlockingOrder, **whoever owns them**, gathered front to back into a list and sent from its back: the last of the side first, one to each scored neighbour in turn.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4D84C0-0x4D8536 read live 2026-11-18; the recording wr15's aimove.txt (main-thread SOV): 119. and 125. Strelkovaya sent from 1809 at tick 60807903, 64. at 60807904. Wrong if a fall-back is seen sending more defenders than outside neighbours while an inside neighbour is scored.
